1	# Business Requirements Document: Credit Control
2	
3	| | |
4	|---|---|
5	| Prepared for | Finance Director |
6	| Prepared by | Business Analyst, Finance |
7	| Version | 1.0 (draft for sign-off) |
8	| Status | For review by Finance, Sales and IT |
9	
10	## 1. Purpose
11	
12	This document sets out what the business needs from a credit control capability in our ERP system. Today credit control lives in a spreadsheet and in the head of our credit controller. The board has asked that it move into the ERP, so that the same rules are applied to every customer every time, so that sales staff and customers cannot get around them, and so that our auditors can see what was decided, by whom and when.
13	
14	The document describes the business behaviour we want. It does not say how the software should be built.
15	
16	## 2. Background
17	
18	We are a wholesale distributor with about 900 trade customers on account. Customers are billed in several currencies. Orders reach us in four main ways: entered by our sales office, placed by customers through our web shop, sent to us electronically by larger customers, and raised automatically from standing monthly orders.
19	
20	Last financial year our bad debt write-offs were well above what the board considers acceptable. A review found the main causes were:
21	
22	- Customers kept being supplied after they had stopped paying, because the "stop list" was a spreadsheet that the sales office and the web shop did not check.
23	- Credit limits were set once when the account was opened and rarely looked at again.
24	- Reminder letters were sent irregularly, depending on how busy the credit controller was.
25	- We charged no interest or late fees, so slow payers had no reason to pay on time.
26	- Write-offs were posted inconsistently, and at year end the auditors had trouble matching the sales ledger to the general ledger and to the decisions behind each write-off.
27	
28	We already use the ERP for sales orders, invoicing, customer accounts, statements and the general ledger, so the credit control work should sit there too.
29	
30	## 3. Stakeholders
31	
32	| Stakeholder | Interest |
33	|---|---|
34	| Finance Director (sponsor) | Lower bad debt, consistent control, a clean audit. |
35	| Maria, Credit Controller | Runs credit control day to day: reviews, stops, reminders, charges, write-offs. |
36	| Deputy Credit Controller | Covers for Maria with the same authority. |
37	| Financial Accountant | Month-end close; the ledger must agree with customer accounts. |
38	| Sales Manager and sales reps | Need to know which of their customers are on stop or on watch; must not be able to override it. |
39	| Sales office / order entry | Must be stopped from processing orders for customers on stop. |
40	| Customers | See their own reminders, interest and fees; receive reminder letters by email. |
41	| External auditors | Need a trail of credit decisions, charges and write-offs. |
42	| IT / system administrator | Installs and configures the change on our live system. |
43	
44	## 4. Scope
45	
46	### 4.1 In scope
47	
48	1. Periodic credit reviews of customers, recording the outcome, notes and the next review date.
49	2. Putting customers "on stop" (also called "on hold" or "frozen") and taking them off stop.
50	3. A softer "watch" status for customers we are worried about but still supply.
51	4. Overdue reminder letters ("chasers", "dunning letters") in escalating stages, sent by email.
52	5. Interest and/or late fees on overdue balances, charged at month end.
53	6. Writing off bad debts.
54	7. A report of customers due a credit review and customers over their credit limit.
55	8. Sales reps seeing only their own customers' credit information.
56	9. Customers seeing their own reminders and charges in the customer portal.
57	10. Month-end agreement between the general ledger and customer accounts.
58	11. Working on both our existing live system and on any new installation.
59	12. Updating the staff guide.
60	
61	### 4.2 Out of scope
62	
63	- Credit insurance and external credit-reference agency feeds.
64	- Debt collection agencies and legal proceedings (we will continue to handle these outside the system, though we want a note of them against the customer).
65	- Changes to how customers pay us, or to cash allocation.
66	- Customer credit applications and account opening.
67	- Supplier (purchase ledger) side.
68	- Changes to price lists, discounts or sales commissions.
69	
70	## 5. Business Requirements
71	
72	### 5.1 Credit reviews
73	
74	- **BR-01** Credit control must be able to record a credit review against any customer. A review records the date, who did it, the outcome (for example: limit confirmed, limit raised, limit reduced, put on watch, put on stop), any new credit limit, free-text notes and the next review date.
75	- **BR-02** Every customer on account must have a next review date. New customers get one automatically when their account is opened, based on a standard review period set by Finance (we expect 12 months, and shorter for higher-risk customers).
76	- **BR-03** The full history of reviews for a customer must be kept and viewable. Past reviews cannot be changed or deleted.
77	- **BR-04** When a review changes the credit limit, the customer's limit must update as part of the review, so the limit and the reason for it are always recorded together.
78	
79	### 5.2 Stop and watch
80	
81	- **BR-05** Credit control must be able to put a customer on stop, with a reason, and take them off stop, with a reason. Each change records who did it and when.
82	- **BR-06** While a customer is on stop, no new orders may be accepted or released for them, by any route: the sales office, the web shop, electronic orders and standing monthly orders. Goods must not be dispatched or invoiced on existing orders taken before the stop, unless credit control releases them.
83	- **BR-07** Only the credit controller and the deputy (and the Finance Director) may put customers on or off stop, or change credit limits. Sales reps and sales office staff must not be able to.
84	- **BR-08** Credit control must be able to put a customer on "watch". A customer on watch can still be supplied, but anyone taking an order for them must be clearly warned, and credit control should be able to see orders taken for watched customers.
85	- **BR-09** A customer's credit status (normal, watch or on stop) must be clearly visible wherever staff look at that customer or take an order for them.
86	- **BR-10** Orders that would take a customer over their credit limit must be held for credit control's approval rather than accepted outright. (Today reps "just put it through".)
87	- **BR-11** Where a customer has asked for or been told about a stop, the customer should see in the web shop that their account is on hold and should contact us, rather than having orders silently fail.
88	
89	### 5.3 Reminder letters (dunning)
90	
91	- **BR-12** The system must send overdue reminder letters in escalating stages. We expect three stages to start with: a polite reminder, a firmer second letter, and a final notice warning that the account will be put on stop and charges applied. Finance must be able to set the number of stages, how many days overdue triggers each stage and the wording of each letter.
92	- **BR-13** Reminders must go by email to the customer's accounts contact. Customers with no email address must be listed so that credit control can post the letter.
93	- **BR-14** Reminders are produced in a regular run (we expect weekly) started by credit control. Before sending, credit control must be able to see who will get which letter and leave out particular customers (for example, where a payment has been promised or there is a dispute).
94	- **BR-15** A customer should only move up a stage if they are still overdue; a customer who pays must not get the next letter. A customer must not receive the same stage twice in a short time.
95	- **BR-16** Every reminder sent must be recorded against the customer: the date, the stage, what invoices it covered and the amount.
96	- **BR-17** Reminders must be in the customer's own currency and show their overdue invoices.
97	- **BR-18** Credit control should be able to mark an invoice as disputed, so that it is not chased and not charged interest until the dispute is settled.
98	
99	### 5.4 Interest and late fees
100	
101	- **BR-19** At month end the system must be able to charge interest on overdue balances, a fixed late fee, or both. Finance must be able to set the interest rate, the fee amount and how many days overdue a balance must be before it is charged.
102	- **BR-20** It must be possible to exempt individual customers from interest and/or fees (for example, key accounts or those with agreed payment plans).
103	- **BR-21** Charges must be raised in the customer's own currency and must appear on the customer's account and their next statement as separate, clearly described items.
104	- **BR-22** Before charges are posted, credit control must be able to see a list of what will be charged to whom, and confirm it. The same month must not be charged twice.
105	- **BR-23** Interest and fees must post to the general ledger to the income accounts that Finance chooses.
106	- **BR-24** Credit control must be able to waive (reverse) a charge for a customer, with a reason, and the reversal must also reach the ledger.
107	
108	### 5.5 Bad debt write-off
109	
110	- **BR-25** Credit control must be able to write off all or part of a customer's unpaid balance as a bad debt, with a reason.
111	- **BR-26** Write-offs above an amount set by Finance must be approved by the Finance Director before they take effect.
112	- **BR-27** A write-off must reduce the customer's balance and post to the bad debt account in the general ledger, including any currency difference.
113	- **BR-28** When a customer has a debt written off, the customer should be put on stop automatically, unless credit control decides otherwise.
114	- **BR-29** There must be a report of write-offs over a period, showing customer, amount, reason, who did it and who approved it.
115	
116	### 5.6 Reporting
117	
118	- **BR-30** A credit control report must list customers who are due or overdue for a credit review, customers over their credit limit (and by how much), and customers on watch or on stop. It must be filterable by sales rep and by currency, and totals must be shown in our home currency.
119	- **BR-31** The aged debt report must show each customer's credit status, credit limit and the last reminder stage sent.
120	- **BR-32** All credit control actions (reviews, stop/watch changes, limit changes, reminders, charges, waivers and write-offs) must be visible as a history per customer that the auditors can inspect.
121	
122	### 5.7 Sales reps
123	
124	- **BR-33** Sales reps must see credit information (status, limit, balance, overdue amounts, reminders) only for their own customers, not for other reps' customers.
125	- **BR-34** Reps can see but not change credit status or limits.
126	
127	### 5.8 Customer portal
128	
129	- **BR-35** Customers who log in to the portal must be able to see the reminder letters we have sent them and the interest and fees charged to their account, along with their balance.
130	- **BR-36** A customer must only ever see their own account.
131	
132	### 5.9 Month end and the ledger
133	
134	- **BR-37** At month end the total of all customer balances must agree with the trade debtors control account in the general ledger, after interest, fees, waivers and write-offs have been posted.
135	- **BR-38** If they do not agree, Finance must be able to find out why from the system.
136	
137	### 5.10 Installation and rollout
138	
139	- **BR-39** The capability must work on our existing live system, with all our existing customers, balances and history, as well as on a brand-new installation.
140	- **BR-40** On go-live every existing customer starts as "normal", with a next review date set by Finance, unless credit control loads their current status from the spreadsheet. Existing customers who are on the spreadsheet stop list today must be on stop in the system from day one.
141	- **BR-41** Nothing in the new capability should change how existing invoices, statements or postings behave for customers who are not overdue.
142	
143	### 5.11 Documentation and training
144	
145	- **BR-42** The staff guide must be updated to explain credit reviews, stop and watch, the reminder run, month-end charges, write-offs and the credit control report.
146	- **BR-43** Sales staff need a short note on what "watch" and "stop" mean for them and who to contact.
147	
148	## 6. User Stories
149	
150	1. **As Maria (credit controller)**, I want to see every Monday which customers are due a review or over their limit, so that I can work through them in order and nothing slips.
151	2. **As Maria**, I want to put a customer on stop once, and know that the sales office, the web shop, EDI orders and the standing orders are all blocked, so that I don't have to phone round.
152	3. **As the deputy credit controller**, I want the same powers and the same history as Maria, so that I can cover her holidays without asking her what she agreed with whom.
153	4. **As a sales rep**, I want to see when one of my customers is on watch or on stop, and why, so that I can talk to the customer before they place an order.
154	5. **As Maria**, I want the weekly reminder run to email the right letter at the right stage to each overdue customer, after I've had a chance to take out the ones I'm already talking to.
155	6. **As the Financial Accountant**, I want month-end interest and fees to post themselves to the ledger, so that the debtors control account agrees with the customer balances without manual journals.
156	7. **As the Finance Director**, I want to approve large write-offs before they go through, so that I know what bad debt we are taking.
157	8. **As a customer**, I want to see in the portal the reminders and charges on my account, so that I understand what I owe and why.
158	9. **As the external auditor**, I want to see for any customer who changed their credit limit or status, when and why, so that I can test the credit control process.
159	
160	## 7. Acceptance Criteria (business terms)
161	
162	- **AC-01** Maria records a review on a customer, raising their limit and setting next review in six months. The new limit applies straight away, and the review, with her notes, appears in the customer's history. The customer drops off the "due for review" list and reappears when the next date comes round.
163	- **AC-02** A customer is put on stop. An order for them cannot be completed in the sales office, through the web shop, electronically or from their standing order. When they are taken off stop, orders go through again. Both changes appear in their history with reasons.
164	- **AC-03** A sales rep tries to take a customer off stop or raise a limit and cannot.
165	- **AC-04** A customer on watch places an order: it is accepted, the person taking it sees a warning, and the order shows on credit control's list.
166	- **AC-05** An order that would take a customer over their limit is held and only released when credit control approves it.
167	- **AC-06** In the reminder run, a customer 35 days overdue gets the first letter by email; the next run, if still unpaid and past the second threshold, they get the second letter; if they pay in between, they get nothing. A customer marked disputed gets no letter. Every letter sent shows on the customer's account history and in their portal.
168	- **AC-07** At month end, an overdue customer is charged interest at the set rate and the set late fee in their own currency; an exempt customer is not charged; running the charges again for the same month charges nobody twice. The charges appear on the customer's statement and in the portal.
169	- **AC-08** After month-end charges, waivers and write-offs, the total of customer balances equals the debtors control account in the general ledger.
170	- **AC-09** A write-off below the approval amount reduces the customer's balance and appears in the bad debt account; one above it does nothing until the Finance Director approves it. The customer is put on stop.
171	- **AC-10** Rep A sees credit details for her customers and none for Rep B's customers. Customer X in the portal sees only Customer X's reminders and charges.
172	- **AC-11** After go-live on the live system, all existing customers, balances and history are intact, every customer has a next review date, and everyone on the old spreadsheet stop list is on stop.
173	- **AC-12** The updated staff guide covers every item in section 4.1 and has been read and agreed by Maria and the Sales Manager.
174	
175	## 8. Assumptions
176	
177	- Customers' accounts contact email addresses are mostly up to date; credit control will clean up the rest before go-live.
178	- Each customer already has a single sales rep assigned.
179	- Our terms and conditions allow us to charge interest and late fees; Legal will confirm the wording for letters.
180	- Credit control will provide the current stop list and credit limits from the spreadsheet for go-live.
181	
182	## 9. Open Questions
183	
184	1. Interest: a simple annual rate on overdue balances, or a statutory late-payment rate? Does it differ by currency or country?
185	2. Late fee: one flat fee per month, or a fee per overdue invoice? Should it vary by currency?
186	3. Do we charge interest on interest and fees that are themselves overdue?
187	4. Should a customer be put on stop automatically after the final reminder, or only flagged for Maria to decide?
188	5. How should over-limit orders from the web shop and standing orders be handled: held for approval, or rejected with a message to the customer?
189	6. What is the approval threshold for write-offs, and does the Financial Accountant also need to sign off?
190	7. If a written-off debt is later paid, how do we want it shown?
191	8. Should reps be told the reason for a stop, or only that the customer is on stop?
192	9. Do we need the reminder letters in languages other than English for overseas customers?
193	10. Should customers be able to see "watch" status in the portal? (Our view: no.)
194	11. Who covers credit decisions when both Maria and her deputy are away?
195	12. Do head-office/branch customer groups share one credit limit, or does each branch have its own?

9. **As the external auditor**, I want to see for any customer who changed their credit limit or status, when and why, so that I can test the credit control process.

## 7. Acceptance Criteria (business terms)

- **AC-01** Maria records a review on a customer, raising their limit and setting next review in six months. The new limit applies straight away, and the review, with her notes, appears in the customer's history. The customer drops off the "due for review" list and reappears when the next date comes round.
- **AC-02** A customer is put on stop. An order for them cannot be completed in the sales office, through the web shop, electronically or from their standing order. When they are taken off stop, orders go through again. Both changes appear in their history with reasons.
- **AC-03** A sales rep tries to take a customer off stop or raise a limit and cannot.
- **AC-04** A customer on watch places an order: it is accepted, the person taking it sees a warning, and the order shows on credit control's list.
- **AC-05** An order that would take a customer over their limit is held and only released when credit control approves it.
- **AC-06** In the reminder run, a customer 35 days overdue gets the first letter by email; the next run, if still unpaid and past the second threshold, they get the second letter; if they pay in between, they get nothing. A customer marked disputed gets no letter. Every letter sent shows on the customer's account history and in their portal.
- **AC-07** At month end, an overdue customer is charged interest at the set rate and the set late fee in their own currency; an exempt customer is not charged; running the charges again for the same month charges nobody twice. The charges appear on the customer's statement and in the portal.
- **AC-08** After month-end charges, waivers and write-offs, the total of customer balances equals the debtors control account in the general ledger.
- **AC-09** A write-off below the approval amount reduces the customer's balance and appears in the bad debt account; one above it does nothing until the Finance Director approves it. The customer is put on stop.
- **AC-10** Rep A sees credit details for her customers and none for Rep B's customers. Customer X in the portal sees only Customer X's reminders and charges.
- **AC-11** After go-live on the live system, all existing customers, balances and history are intact, every customer has a next review date, and everyone on the old spreadsheet stop list is on stop.
- **AC-12** The updated staff guide covers every item in section 4.1 and has been read and agreed by Maria and the Sales Manager.

## 8. Assumptions

- Customers' accounts contact email addresses are mostly up to date; credit control will clean up the rest before go-live.
- Each customer already has a single sales rep assigned.
- Our terms and conditions allow us to charge interest and late fees; Legal will confirm the wording for letters.
- Credit control will provide the current stop list and credit limits from the spreadsheet for go-live.

## 9. Open Questions

1. Interest: a simple annual rate on overdue balances, or a statutory late-payment rate? Does it differ by currency or country?
2. Late fee: one flat fee per month, or a fee per overdue invoice? Should it vary by currency?
3. Do we charge interest on interest and fees that are themselves overdue?
4. Should a customer be put on stop automatically after the final reminder, or only flagged for Maria to decide?
5. How should over-limit orders from the web shop and standing orders be handled: held for approval, or rejected with a message to the customer?
6. What is the approval threshold for write-offs, and does the Financial Accountant also need to sign off?
7. If a written-off debt is later paid, how do we want it shown?
8. Should reps be told the reason for a stop, or only that the customer is on stop?
9. Do we need the reminder letters in languages other than English for overseas customers?
10. Should customers be able to see "watch" status in the portal? (Our view: no.)
11. Who covers credit decisions when both Maria and her deputy are away?
12. Do head-office/branch customer groups share one credit limit, or does each branch have its own?

(2,21,'Second reminder: overdue invoices on your account','Dear {customer},\n\nWe wrote to you recently about the overdue invoices listed below and have not yet received payment. <?php

// CREDIT CONTROL
//
// Reviews, stop and watch, dunning letters, month end interest and late fees, bad debt write offs and the
// audit trail that goes with them. Customer stop and watch are NOT a new field on debtorsmaster - they are
// the existing credit status (holdreasons.dissallowinvoices: 0 = normal, 1 = on stop, 2 = on watch).
// Everything new lives in its own tables, so existing customers, transactions and statements are untouched.

// 1. tables
CreateTable('debtorcredit', "CREATE TABLE `debtorcredit` (
  `debtorno` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `nextreviewdate` date NOT NULL DEFAULT '1000-01-01',
  `exemptinterest` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `exemptfees` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `collectionnote` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`debtorno`),
  KEY `nextreviewdate` (`nextreviewdate`)
)");

CreateTable('creditlog', "CREATE TABLE `creditlog` (
  `id` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `debtorno` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `eventdate` datetime NOT NULL,
  `userid` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `eventtype` varchar(12) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `description` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `amount` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `currcode` char(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `reference` varchar(50) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `debtorno` (`debtorno`,`eventdate`),
  KEY `eventtype` (`eventtype`)
)");

CreateTable('creditreviews', "CREATE TABLE `creditreviews` (
  `id` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `debtorno` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `reviewdate` date NOT NULL DEFAULT '1000-01-01',
  `userid` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `outcome` varchar(12) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `oldlimit` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `newlimit` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `notes` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `nextreviewdate` date NOT NULL DEFAULT '1000-01-01',
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `debtorno` (`debtorno`,`reviewdate`)
)");

CreateTable('dunningstages', "CREATE TABLE `dunningstages` (
  `stage` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '1',
  `daysoverdue` smallint NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `subject` varchar(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `body` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`stage`)
)");

CreateTable('dunningletters', "CREATE TABLE `dunningletters` (
  `id` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `debtorno` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `stage` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '1',
  `sentdate` datetime NOT NULL,
  `userid` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `currcode` char(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `amount` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `sentto` varchar(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `method` char(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'E',
  `lettertext` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `debtorno` (`debtorno`,`sentdate`)
)");

CreateTable('dunninglettersdetail', "CREATE TABLE `dunninglettersdetail` (
  `letterid` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `transid` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `amount` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  PRIMARY KEY (`letterid`,`transid`),
  KEY `transid` (`transid`)
)");

CreateTable('creditdisputes', "CREATE TABLE `creditdisputes` (
  `transid` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `debtorno` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `disputedate` datetime NOT NULL,
  `userid` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `reason` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `resolved` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `resolvedate` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `resolvedby` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  PRIMARY KEY (`transid`),
  KEY `debtorno` (`debtorno`)
)");

CreateTable('creditorderholds', "CREATE TABLE `creditorderholds` (
  `orderno` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `debtorno` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `reason` varchar(100) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `status` char(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'H',
  `heldon` datetime NOT NULL,
  `releasedby` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `releasedon` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `note` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`orderno`),
  KEY `debtorno` (`debtorno`),
  KEY `status` (`status`)
)");

CreateTable('latecharges', "CREATE TABLE `latecharges` (
  `id` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `debtorno` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `chargemonth` char(7) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `chargetype` char(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'I',
  `amount` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `basis` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `currcode` char(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `transid` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `transno` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `chargedate` date NOT NULL DEFAULT '1000-01-01',
  `userid` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `status` char(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'P',
  `waivetransno` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `waivedby` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `waiveddate` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `waivereason` varchar(255) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  UNIQUE KEY `onceamonth` (`debtorno`,`chargemonth`,`chargetype`),
  KEY `transid` (`transid`)
)");

CreateTable('writeoffs', "CREATE TABLE `writeoffs` (
  `id` int NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `debtorno` varchar(10) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `currcode` char(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `amount` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `localamount` double NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `reason` text DEFAULT NULL,
  `requestedby` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `requestdate` datetime NOT NULL,
  `status` char(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'P',
  `approvedby` varchar(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `approveddate` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `decisionnote` varchar(255) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  `transno` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `putonstop` tinyint NOT NULL DEFAULT '1',
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `debtorno` (`debtorno`),
  KEY `status` (`status`),
  KEY `requestdate` (`requestdate`)
)");

// 2. new debtor transaction types - kept apart from sales invoices and credit notes so that statements say
// what the item is, and sales reports that look at invoices and credit notes are not polluted
NewSysType(51, 'Late Payment Interest');
NewSysType(52, 'Late Payment Fee');
NewSysType(53, 'Bad Debt Write Off');
NewSysType(54, 'Late Charge Waiver');

// 3. security tokens: 21 credit controller / deputy, 22 finance director (settings and large write off approval)
NewSecurityToken(21, 'Credit Control');
NewSecurityToken(22, 'Credit Control - Finance Director');
InsertRecord('securitygroups', array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array(6, 21), array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array(6, 21));
InsertRecord('securitygroups', array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array(8, 21), array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array(8, 21));
InsertRecord('securitygroups', array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array(8, 22), array('secroleid', 'tokenid'), array(8, 22));

// 4. scripts and menu items
NewScript('CreditControlCustomer.php', 21);
NewScript('CreditControlReminders.php', 21);
NewScript('CreditControlCharges.php', 21);
NewScript('CreditControlWriteOffs.php', 21);
NewScript('CreditControlOrders.php', 21);
NewScript('CreditControlImport.php', 21);
NewScript('CreditControlSetup.php', 22);
NewScript('CreditControlReport.php', 2);
NewScript('CustomerCreditAccount.php', 1);

// function NewMenuItem($Link, $Section, $Caption, $URL, $Sequence)
NewMenuItem('AR', 'Transactions', __('Credit Control Reminder Run'), '/CreditControlReminders.php', 50);
NewMenuItem('AR', 'Transactions', __('Month End Interest and Late Fees'), '/CreditControlCharges.php', 51);
NewMenuItem('AR', 'Transactions', __('Bad Debt Write Offs'), '/CreditControlWriteOffs.php', 52);
NewMenuItem('AR', 'Transactions', __('Credit Control Orders'), '/CreditControlOrders.php', 53);
NewMenuItem('AR', 'Reports', __('Credit Control Report'), '/CreditControlReport.php', 50);
NewMenuItem('AR', 'Reports', __('Customer Credit Account'), '/CustomerCreditAccount.php', 55);
NewMenuItem('AR', 'Maintenance', __('Customer Credit File'), '/CreditControlCustomer.php', 50);
NewMenuItem('AR', 'Maintenance', __('Load Credit Status from .csv file'), '/CreditControlImport.php', 51);
NewMenuItem('AR', 'Maintenance', __('Credit Control Settings'), '/CreditControlSetup.php', 52);

// 5. credit statuses. Stop = a credit status that disallows invoices (1), watch = one that only warns (2).
// Find or create the three statuses credit control switches customers between, and remember their codes.
$Result = DB_query("SELECT confvalue FROM config WHERE confname='CreditControlStopReason'");
if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 0) {
	$Codes = array();
	$Wanted = array('Normal' => array(0, __('Good History')),
					'Watch' => array(2, __('On Watch')),
					'Stop' => array(1, __('On Stop')));
	foreach ($Wanted as $Key => $Status) {
		$Code = false;
		if ($Key == 'Normal') {
			// any existing status that allows invoicing will do for normal
			$ReasonResult = DB_query("SELECT reasoncode FROM holdreasons WHERE dissallowinvoices=0 ORDER BY reasoncode LIMIT 1");
			if (DB_num_rows($ReasonResult) == 1) {
				$ReasonRow = DB_fetch_row($ReasonResult);
				$Code = $ReasonRow[0];
			}
		} else {
			// watch and stop get their own, clearly named, statuses so the meaning of existing ones is not changed
			$ReasonResult = DB_query("SELECT reasoncode FROM holdreasons WHERE dissallowinvoices='" . $Status[0] . "' AND reasondescription='" . DB_escape_string($Status[1]) . "' ORDER BY reasoncode LIMIT 1");
			if (DB_num_rows($ReasonResult) == 1) {
				$ReasonRow = DB_fetch_row($ReasonResult);
				$Code = $ReasonRow[0];
			}
		}
		if ($Code === false) {
			// first free code at or below 98 (CreditStatus.php only allows codes up to 99)
			$Code = 98;
			while ($Code > 0) {
				$ReasonResult = DB_query("SELECT reasoncode FROM holdreasons WHERE reasoncode='" . $Code . "'");
				if (DB_num_rows($ReasonResult) == 0) {
					break;
				}
				$Code--;
			}
			InsertRecord('holdreasons', array('reasoncode'), array($Code), array('reasoncode', 'reasondescription', 'dissallowinvoices'), array($Code, $Status[1], $Status[0]));
		}
		$Codes[$Key] = $Code;
	}
	NewConfigValue('CreditControlNormalReason', $Codes['Normal']);
	NewConfigValue('CreditControlWatchReason', $Codes['Watch']);
	NewConfigValue('CreditControlStopReason', $Codes['Stop']);
}

// 6. settings Finance can change in Credit Control Settings
NewConfigValue('CreditControlReviewMonths', '12');
NewConfigValue('CreditControlInterestRate', '0');
NewConfigValue('CreditControlLateFee', '0');
NewConfigValue('CreditControlGraceDays', '30');
NewConfigValue('CreditControlInterestAct', '');
NewConfigValue('CreditControlFeeAct', '');
NewConfigValue('CreditControlBadDebtAct', '');
NewConfigValue('CreditControlWriteOffLimit', '500');
NewConfigValue('CreditControlReminderGapDays', '7');

// 7. starter dunning letters - three stages, Finance can change the number, timing and wording
$Result = DB_query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dunningstages");
$Row = DB_fetch_row($Result);
if ($Row[0] == 0) {
	InsertRecord('dunningstages', array('stage'), array(1), array('stage', 'daysoverdue', 'subject', 'body'), array(1, 7, 'Reminder: overdue invoices on your account', "Dear {customer},\n\nOur records show that the invoices listed below are now overdue for payment. If you have already paid them, please ignore this letter and accept our thanks.\n\n{invoices}\n\nTotal overdue: {currency} {total}\n\nKind regards,\n{company} Credit Control"));
	InsertRecord('dunningstages', array('stage'), array(2), array('stage', 'daysoverdue', 'subject', 'body'), array(2, 21, 'Second reminder: overdue invoices on your account', "Dear {customer},\n\nWe wrote to you recently about the overdue invoices listed below and have not yet received payment. Please arrange payment immediately or contact us if there is a problem.\n\n{invoices}\n\nTotal overdue: {currency} {total}\n\nKind regards,\n{company} Credit Control"));
	InsertRecord('dunningstages', array('stage'), array(3), array('stage', 'daysoverdue', 'subject', 'body'), array(3, 35, 'FINAL NOTICE: overdue invoices on your account', "Dear {customer},\n\nThis is our final notice. The invoices listed below remain unpaid. Unless payment is received within 7 days your account will be placed on stop, no further orders can be supplied, and interest and late payment fees will be applied in line with our terms and conditions.\n\n{invoices}\n\nTotal overdue: {currency} {total}\n\nKind regards,\n{company} Credit Control"));
}

// 8. every existing customer gets a next review date (a standard period from today - Finance can re-date them
// in Credit Control Settings or load dates from the spreadsheet) and starts with whatever credit status it has now
$Result = DB_query("SELECT confvalue FROM config WHERE confname='CreditControlReviewMonths'");
$Row = DB_fetch_row($Result);
$ReviewMonths = (int) $Row[0];
if ($ReviewMonths < 1) {
	$ReviewMonths = 12;
}
$Response = executeSQL("INSERT INTO debtorcredit (debtorno, nextreviewdate)
						SELECT debtorno, DATE_ADD(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL " . $ReviewMonths . " MONTH)
						FROM debtorsmaster
						WHERE debtorno NOT IN (SELECT debtorno FROM debtorcredit)", false);
if ($Response == 0) {
	OutputResult(__('Next credit review dates have been set for existing customers'), 'success');
} else {
	OutputResult(__('Next credit review dates could not be set for existing customers'), 'error');
}

// 9. order entry can now hold an order that would take the customer over their limit for credit control to approve
// (Check Credit Limits = 3). Existing systems keep their current setting - change it in Configuration > System Parameters.

if ($_SESSION['Updates']['Errors'] == 0) {
	UpdateDBNo(basename(__FILE__, '.php'), __('Credit control: reviews, stop and watch, reminder letters, interest and late fees, write offs'));
}

<?php

/* Credit control functions shared by the credit control pages, order entry, invoicing and the API.

Needs includes/SQL_CommonFunctions.php and includes/DateFunctions.php to have been loaded (GetNextTransNo, GetPeriod).

Credit status is the existing customer credit status (debtorsmaster.holdreason -> holdreasons.dissallowinvoices):
	0 = normal, 1 = on stop (no new orders, no dispatch or invoicing), 2 = on watch (supplied, but flagged).

Debtor transaction types used for charges and write offs - they are kept apart from sales invoices (10) and credit
notes (11) so statements describe them properly. 51 and 52 are debits, 53 and 54 are credits. */

define('CC_TYPE_INTEREST', 51);
define('CC_TYPE_FEE', 52);
define('CC_TYPE_WRITEOFF', 53);
define('CC_TYPE_WAIVER', 54);

/* The token that lets a user act as credit control, and the finance director's token */
define('CC_TOKEN_CONTROL', 21);
define('CC_TOKEN_FINANCE_DIRECTOR', 22);

function CreditControlIsController() {
	return isset($_SESSION['AllowedPageSecurityTokens']) and in_array(CC_TOKEN_CONTROL, $_SESSION['AllowedPageSecurityTokens']);
}

function CreditControlIsFinanceDirector() {
	return isset($_SESSION['AllowedPageSecurityTokens']) and in_array(CC_TOKEN_FINANCE_DIRECTOR, $_SESSION['AllowedPageSecurityTokens']);
}

/* The credit control settings from the config table, with defaults for a database that has not been set up.
Read from the database rather than the session so that the API, cron scripts and a just-changed setting all see the same values */
function CreditControlSettings($Refresh = false) {
	static $Settings = null;
	if ($Settings === null or $Refresh) {
		$Settings = array('CreditControlReviewMonths' => '12',
						'CreditControlNormalReason' => '',
						'CreditControlWatchReason' => '',
						'CreditControlStopReason' => '',
						'CreditControlInterestRate' => '0',
						'CreditControlLateFee' => '0',
						'CreditControlGraceDays' => '30',
						'CreditControlInterestAct' => '',
						'CreditControlFeeAct' => '',
						'CreditControlBadDebtAct' => '',
						'CreditControlWriteOffLimit' => '500',
						'CreditControlReminderGapDays' => '7');
		$Result = DB_query("SELECT confname, confvalue FROM config WHERE confname LIKE 'CreditControl%'");
		while ($MyRow = DB_fetch_array($Result)) {
			$Settings[$MyRow['confname']] = $MyRow['confvalue'];
		}
	}
	return $Settings;
}

/* Record something credit control did. This is the audit trail the auditors look at - rows are only ever added */
function CreditControlLog($DebtorNo, $EventType, $Description, $Amount = 0, $CurrCode = '', $Reference = '') {
	$UserID = isset($_SESSION['UserID']) ? $_SESSION['UserID'] : 'system';
	$SQL = "INSERT INTO creditlog (debtorno,
									eventdate,
									userid,
									eventtype,
									description,
									amount,
									currcode,
									reference)
				VALUES ('" . $DebtorNo . "',
						NOW(),
						'" . $UserID . "',
						'" . $EventType . "',
						'" . DB_escape_string($Description) . "',
						'" . $Amount . "',
						'" . $CurrCode . "',
						'" . DB_escape_string(mb_substr($Reference, 0, 50)) . "')";
	DB_query($SQL, __('The credit control history could not be updated because'));
}

/* The credit status of a customer as array('Status' => N|W|S, 'Reason' => text, 'ReasonCode' => code) */
function CreditControlGetStatus($DebtorNo) {
	$SQL = "SELECT debtorsmaster.holdreason,
					holdreasons.dissallowinvoices,
					holdreasons.reasondescription
			FROM debtorsmaster
			LEFT JOIN holdreasons
				ON debtorsmaster.holdreason=holdreasons.reasoncode
			WHERE debtorsmaster.debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "'";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_array($Result);
	$Status = 'N';
	if ($MyRow['dissallowinvoices'] == 1) {
		$Status = 'S';
	} elseif ($MyRow['dissallowinvoices'] == 2) {
		$Status = 'W';
	}
	return array('Status' => $Status,
				'Reason' => $MyRow['reasondescription'],
				'ReasonCode' => $MyRow['holdreason']);
}

function CreditControlStatusText($Status) {
	if ($Status == 'S') {
		return __('On stop');
	} elseif ($Status == 'W') {
		return __('On watch');
	}
	return __('Normal');
}

function CreditControlIsOnStop($DebtorNo) {
	$Status = CreditControlGetStatus($DebtorNo);
	return ($Status['Status'] == 'S');
}

/* Move a customer to normal, watch or stop, and record why. Call inside the caller's transaction.
Returns false when no credit status has been set up for the requested state. */
function CreditControlSetStatus($DebtorNo, $NewStatus, $Reason) {
	$Settings = CreditControlSettings();
	if ($NewStatus == 'S') {
		$Code = $Settings['CreditControlStopReason'];
	} elseif ($NewStatus == 'W') {
		$Code = $Settings['CreditControlWatchReason'];
	} else {
		$Code = $Settings['CreditControlNormalReason'];
	}
	if ($Code === '') {
		return false;
	}
	$Old = CreditControlGetStatus($DebtorNo);
	DB_query("UPDATE debtorsmaster SET holdreason='" . $Code . "' WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "'",
		__('The credit status of the customer could not be updated because'));
	CreditControlLog($DebtorNo,
		'STATUS',
		CreditControlStatusText($Old['Status']) . ' -> ' . CreditControlStatusText($NewStatus) . ': ' . $Reason);
	return true;
}

/* Give a customer a next review date if it does not have one - called when customers are created */
function CreditControlNewCustomer($DebtorNo) {
	$Settings = CreditControlSettings();
	$Months = (int) $Settings['CreditControlReviewMonths'];
	if ($Months < 1) {
		$Months = 12;
	}
	DB_query("INSERT INTO debtorcredit (debtorno, nextreviewdate)
				SELECT '" . $DebtorNo . "', DATE_ADD(CURRENT_DATE, INTERVAL " . $Months . " MONTH)
				FROM (SELECT 1) AS dummy
				WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM debtorcredit WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "')");
}

/* '' if the order can be dispatched and invoiced, otherwise the reason it can't be.
An order is stopped when the customer is on stop or the order is being held for credit approval - unless
credit control has released that order. */
function CreditControlOrderInvoiceBlock($OrderNo, $DebtorNo) {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT status FROM creditorderholds WHERE orderno='" . (int) $OrderNo . "'");
	$Hold = DB_fetch_array($Result);
	if ($Hold['status'] == 'R') {
		return '';
	}
	if ($Hold['status'] == 'H') {
		return __('This order is being held for credit control approval and cannot be dispatched or invoiced until credit control releases it');
	}
	if (CreditControlIsOnStop($DebtorNo)) {
		return __('This customer is on stop. Orders cannot be dispatched or invoiced unless credit control releases them');
	}
	return '';
}

/* After an order has been written, hold it for credit control approval if it takes the customer over their credit limit
(only when Check Credit Limits is set to hold orders). Returns true if the order was held. */
function CreditControlHoldOrderIfOverLimit($OrderNo, $DebtorNo) {
	if (!isset($_SESSION['CheckCreditLimits']) or $_SESSION['CheckCreditLimits'] != 3) {
		return false;
	}
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT quotation FROM salesorders WHERE orderno='" . (int) $OrderNo . "'");
	$Order = DB_fetch_array($Result);
	if ($Order['quotation'] != 0) {
		return false;
	}
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT status FROM creditorderholds WHERE orderno='" . (int) $OrderNo . "'");
	if (DB_num_rows($Result) > 0) {
		// already held, or already released by credit control
		return false;
	}
	if (GetCreditAvailable($DebtorNo) >= 0) {
		return false;
	}
	DB_query("INSERT INTO creditorderholds (orderno,
											debtorno,
											reason,
											status,
											heldon)
				VALUES ('" . (int) $OrderNo . "',
						'" . $DebtorNo . "',
						'" . DB_escape_string(__('Over credit limit')) . "',
						'H',
						NOW())",
		__('The credit hold on the order could not be recorded because'));
	CreditControlLog($DebtorNo, 'ORDERHOLD', __('Order held for credit approval - over credit limit'), 0, '', $OrderNo);
	return true;
}

/* SQL for the due date of a debtor transaction, from the customer's payment terms - the same rule as the aged debtors report.
Needs debtortrans and paymentterms in the query. */
function CreditControlDueDateSQL() {
	return "CASE WHEN paymentterms.daysbeforedue > 0
				THEN DATE_ADD(debtortrans.trandate, INTERVAL paymentterms.daysbeforedue DAY)
				ELSE DATE_ADD(LAST_DAY(debtortrans.trandate), INTERVAL paymentterms.dayinfollowingmonth DAY)
			END";
}

/* The debits on a customer's account that are past their due date as at $AsAt (a SQL date).
Disputed items are left out, and so are interest and fees when $IncludeCharges is false (interest is not charged on interest).
Returns rows of id, type, typename, transno, trandate, reference, balance, duedate and daysoverdue. */
function CreditControlOverdueItems($DebtorNo, $AsAt = '', $IncludeCharges = true) {
	if ($AsAt == '') {
		$AsAt = date('Y-m-d');
	}
	$SQL = "SELECT debtortrans.id,
					debtortrans.type,
					systypes.typename,
					debtortrans.transno,
					debtortrans.trandate,
					debtortrans.reference,
					debtortrans.balance,
					" . CreditControlDueDateSQL() . " AS duedate,
					DATEDIFF('" . $AsAt . "', " . CreditControlDueDateSQL() . ") AS daysoverdue
			FROM debtortrans
			INNER JOIN debtorsmaster
				ON debtortrans.debtorno=debtorsmaster.debtorno
			INNER JOIN paymentterms
				ON debtorsmaster.paymentterms=paymentterms.termsindicator
			INNER JOIN systypes
				ON debtortrans.type=systypes.typeid
			LEFT JOIN creditdisputes
				ON creditdisputes.transid=debtortrans.id
				AND creditdisputes.resolved=0
			WHERE debtortrans.debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "'
				AND debtortrans.balance > 0.005
				AND creditdisputes.transid IS NULL";
	if (!$IncludeCharges) {
		$SQL .= " AND debtortrans.type NOT IN (" . CC_TYPE_INTEREST . ", " . CC_TYPE_FEE . ")";
	}
	$SQL .= " HAVING daysoverdue > 0
			ORDER BY debtortrans.trandate, debtortrans.id";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL, __('The overdue items of the customer could not be retrieved because'));
	$Items = array();
	while ($MyRow = DB_fetch_array($Result)) {
		$Items[] = $MyRow;
	}
	return $Items;
}

/* The balance on a customer's account in their own currency (receipts and credit notes not yet allocated are netted off) */
function CreditControlBalance($DebtorNo) {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT SUM(balance) FROM debtortrans WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "'");
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_row($Result);
	return (float) $MyRow[0];
}

/* The reminder stage a customer is at now: the highest stage already sent that covered an item that is still unpaid.
When everything chased has been paid they start again from nothing. */
function CreditControlCurrentStage($DebtorNo) {
	$SQL = "SELECT MAX(dunningletters.stage)
			FROM dunningletters
			INNER JOIN dunninglettersdetail
				ON dunninglettersdetail.letterid=dunningletters.id
			INNER JOIN debtortrans
				ON debtortrans.id=dunninglettersdetail.transid
			WHERE dunningletters.debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "'
				AND debtortrans.balance > 0.005";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);
	$MyRow = DB_fetch_row($Result);
	return (int) $MyRow[0];
}

/* Post one debtor transaction for credit control (interest, fee, waiver or write off) to the customer's account and the GL.
$Amount is positive and in the customer's currency; types 51 and 52 add to what the customer owes, 53 and 54 reduce it.
$GLAccount is the other side of the entry to debtors control. $Rate defaults to the current rate for the customer's currency.
Call inside the caller's transaction. Returns array(id, transno, rate, local) or false if the customer has no branch. */
function CreditControlPostDebtorTrans($Type, $DebtorNo, $Amount, $Narrative, $GLAccount, $TranDate, $Reference = '', $Rate = 0) {
	$SQL = "SELECT debtorsmaster.currcode,
					debtorsmaster.salestype,
					currencies.rate
			FROM debtorsmaster
			INNER JOIN currencies
				ON debtorsmaster.currcode=currencies.currabrev
			WHERE debtorsmaster.debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "'";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);
	$Customer = DB_fetch_array($Result);
	if ($Rate == 0) {
		$Rate = $Customer['rate'];
	}
	// the transaction needs a branch - charges go on the first branch, which also decides the sales person
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT branchcode, salesman FROM custbranch WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "' ORDER BY branchcode LIMIT 1");
	if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 0) {
		return false;
	}
	$Branch = DB_fetch_array($Result);

	$TransNo = GetNextTransNo($Type);
	$PeriodNo = GetPeriod(ConvertSQLDate($TranDate));
	$Debit = ($Type == CC_TYPE_INTEREST or $Type == CC_TYPE_FEE);
	$Signed = $Debit ? $Amount : -$Amount;

	$SQL = "INSERT INTO debtortrans (transno,
									type,
									debtorno,
									branchcode,
									trandate,
									inputdate,
									prd,
									reference,
									tpe,
									order_,
									ovamount,
									ovgst,
									ovfreight,
									ovdiscount,
									rate,
									invtext,
									salesperson)
				VALUES ('" . $TransNo . "',
						'" . $Type . "',
						'" . $DebtorNo . "',
						'" . $Branch['branchcode'] . "',
						'" . $TranDate . "',
						NOW(),
						'" . $PeriodNo . "',
						'" . DB_escape_string(mb_substr($Reference, 0, 50)) . "',
						'" . $Customer['salestype'] . "',
						0,
						'" . $Signed . "',
						0,
						0,
						0,
						'" . $Rate . "',
						'" . DB_escape_string($Narrative) . "',
						'" . $Branch['salesman'] . "')";
	DB_query($SQL, __('CRITICAL ERROR') . '! ' . __('NOTE DOWN THIS ERROR AND SEEK ASSISTANCE') . ': ' . __('The debtor transaction could not be inserted because'));
	$TransID = DB_Last_Insert_ID('debtortrans', 'id');

	$Local = round($Amount / $Rate, $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['decimalplaces']);
	if ($_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['gllink_debtors'] == 1 and $Local != 0) {
		$GLNarrative = mb_substr($DebtorNo . ' - ' . $Narrative, 0, 200);
		$DebtorsAmount = $Debit ? $Local : -$Local;
		$GLSQL = "INSERT INTO gltrans (type, typeno, trandate, periodno, account, narrative, amount)
					VALUES ('" . $Type . "', '" . $TransNo . "', '" . $TranDate . "', '" . $PeriodNo . "',
							'" . $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['debtorsact'] . "', '" . DB_escape_string($GLNarrative) . "', '" . $DebtorsAmount . "')";
		DB_query($GLSQL, __('CRITICAL ERROR') . '! ' . __('NOTE DOWN THIS ERROR AND SEEK ASSISTANCE') . ': ' . __('The debtors control GL posting could not be inserted because'));
		$GLSQL = "INSERT INTO gltrans (type, typeno, trandate, periodno, account, narrative, amount)
					VALUES ('" . $Type . "', '" . $TransNo . "', '" . $TranDate . "', '" . $PeriodNo . "',
							'" . $GLAccount . "', '" . DB_escape_string($GLNarrative) . "', '" . -$DebtorsAmount . "')";
		DB_query($GLSQL, __('CRITICAL ERROR') . '! ' . __('NOTE DOWN THIS ERROR AND SEEK ASSISTANCE') . ': ' . __('The GL posting could not be inserted because'));
	}
	return array('id' => $TransID, 'transno' => $TransNo, 'rate' => $Rate, 'local' => $Local);
}

/* Allocate a credit (write off or waiver) just posted against the customer's debits: the ones in $TargetIDs, or oldest first.
Works the way Customer Allocations does - including the difference on exchange when the debit and the credit are at
different rates, which is posted to the sales exchange difference account so debtors control stays equal to the ledger.
Call inside the caller's transaction. Returns the amount allocated. */
function CreditControlAllocateCredit($CreditID, $DebtorNo, $Amount, $TargetIDs = array()) {
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT type, transno, trandate, rate, prd FROM debtortrans WHERE id='" . $CreditID . "'");
	$Credit = DB_fetch_array($Result);

	$SQL = "SELECT id, rate, balance, alloc
			FROM debtortrans
			WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "'
				AND balance > 0.005
				AND id <> '" . $CreditID . "'";
	if (count($TargetIDs) > 0) {
		$SQL .= " AND id IN (" . implode(',', array_map('intval', $TargetIDs)) . ")";
	}
	$SQL .= " ORDER BY trandate, id";
	$Result = DB_query($SQL);

	$Remaining = $Amount;
	$Allocated = 0;
	$TotalDiff = 0;
	while (($Target = DB_fetch_array($Result)) and $Remaining > 0.005) {
		$ThisAlloc = min($Remaining, $Target['balance']);
		// a +ve amount is a gain, -ve a loss - same as CustomerAllocations.php
		$Diff = ($ThisAlloc / $Credit['rate']) - ($ThisAlloc / $Target['rate']);
		DB_query("INSERT INTO custallocns (datealloc, amt, transid_allocfrom, transid_allocto)
					VALUES (CURRENT_DATE, '" . $ThisAlloc . "', '" . $CreditID . "', '" . $Target['id'] . "')");
		$NewAlloc = $Target['alloc'] + $ThisAlloc;
		$Settled = (abs($Target['balance'] - $ThisAlloc) < 0.005) ? 1 : 0;
		DB_query("UPDATE debtortrans
					SET alloc='" . $NewAlloc . "',
						diffonexch=diffonexch + " . $Diff . ",
						settled='" . $Settled . "'
					WHERE id='" . $Target['id'] . "'");
		$Remaining -= $ThisAlloc;
		$Allocated += $ThisAlloc;
		$TotalDiff += $Diff;
	}
	$Settled = (abs($Amount - $Allocated) < 0.005) ? 1 : 0;
	DB_query("UPDATE debtortrans
				SET alloc='" . -$Allocated . "',
					diffonexch='" . -$TotalDiff . "',
					settled='" . $Settled . "'
				WHERE id='" . $CreditID . "'");

	$Movement = round(-$TotalDiff, $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['decimalplaces']);
	if ($_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['gllink_debtors'] == 1 and $Movement != 0) {
		$GLSQL = "INSERT INTO gltrans (type, typeno, trandate, periodno, account, narrative, amount)
					VALUES ('" . $Credit['type'] . "', '" . $Credit['transno'] . "', '" . $Credit['trandate'] . "', '" . $Credit['prd'] . "',
							'" . $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['salesexchangediffact'] . "', '" . DB_escape_string($DebtorNo . ' - ' . __('Difference on exchange')) . "', '" . $Movement . "')";
		DB_query($GLSQL, __('Could not update sales exchange difference in General Ledger'));
		$GLSQL = "INSERT INTO gltrans (type, typeno, trandate, periodno, account, narrative, amount)
					VALUES ('" . $Credit['type'] . "', '" . $Credit['transno'] . "', '" . $Credit['trandate'] . "', '" . $Credit['prd'] . "',
							'" . $_SESSION['CompanyRecord']['debtorsact'] . "', '" . DB_escape_string($DebtorNo . ' - ' . __('Difference on exchange')) . "', '" . -$Movement . "')";
		DB_query($GLSQL, __('Could not update debtors control in General Ledger'));
	}
	return $Allocated;
}

/* Write off the amount of a pending write off: credit the customer's account, debit the bad debt account, allocate the
credit to the oldest debits, and put the customer on stop unless credit control chose not to. Call inside a transaction.
Returns '' on success or the reason it could not be done. */
function CreditControlPostWriteOff($WriteOffID, $ApprovedBy, $DecisionNote = '') {
	$Settings = CreditControlSettings();
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT * FROM writeoffs WHERE id='" . (int) $WriteOffID . "' AND status='P'");
	if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 0) {
		return __('This write off is not waiting to be posted');
	}
	$WriteOff = DB_fetch_array($Result);
	if ($Settings['CreditControlBadDebtAct'] == '') {
		return __('The bad debt GL account has not been set in the credit control settings');
	}
	if (CreditControlBalance($WriteOff['debtorno']) < $WriteOff['amount'] - 0.005) {
		return __('The customer balance is now less than the amount to write off');
	}
	$Post = CreditControlPostDebtorTrans(CC_TYPE_WRITEOFF,
										$WriteOff['debtorno'],
										$WriteOff['amount'],
										__('Bad debt write off') . ' - ' . $WriteOff['reason'],
										$Settings['CreditControlBadDebtAct'],
										date('Y-m-d'),
										__('Write off') . ' ' . $WriteOff['id']);
	if ($Post === false) {
		return __('The customer has no branch to post the write off to');
	}
	CreditControlAllocateCredit($Post['id'], $WriteOff['debtorno'], $WriteOff['amount']);
	DB_query("UPDATE writeoffs
				SET status='A',
					approvedby='" . $ApprovedBy . "',
					approveddate=NOW(),
					decisionnote='" . DB_escape_string(mb_substr($DecisionNote, 0, 255)) . "',
					transno='" . $Post['transno'] . "',
					localamount='" . $Post['local'] . "'
				WHERE id='" . $WriteOff['id'] . "'");
	CreditControlLog($WriteOff['debtorno'],
		'WRITEOFF',
		__('Bad debt written off') . ': ' . $WriteOff['reason'] . ' (' . __('approved by') . ' ' . $ApprovedBy . ')',
		$WriteOff['amount'],
		$WriteOff['currcode'],
		CC_TYPE_WRITEOFF . '/' . $Post['transno']);
	if ($WriteOff['putonstop'] == 1) {
		$Status = CreditControlGetStatus($WriteOff['debtorno']);
		if ($Status['Status'] != 'S') {
			CreditControlSetStatus($WriteOff['debtorno'], 'S', __('Bad debt written off'));
		}
	}
	return '';
}

/* Waive (reverse) a posted interest or fee charge. Credits the customer, reverses the income posting, allocates the
credit to the charge. Done at the rate the charge was posted at so the ledger comes out exactly. Call inside a transaction.
Returns '' on success or the reason it could not be done. */
function CreditControlWaiveCharge($ChargeID, $Reason) {
	$Settings = CreditControlSettings();
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT * FROM latecharges WHERE id='" . (int) $ChargeID . "' AND status='P'");
	if (DB_num_rows($Result) == 0) {
		return __('This charge has already been waived');
	}
	$Charge = DB_fetch_array($Result);
	$Result = DB_query("SELECT balance, rate FROM debtortrans WHERE id='" . $Charge['transid'] . "'");
	$Trans = DB_fetch_array($Result);
	if (abs($Trans['balance'] - $Charge['amount']) > 0.005) {
		return __('This charge has been paid or part paid and cannot be waived');
	}
	$Account = ($Charge['chargetype'] == 'I') ? $Settings['CreditControlInterestAct'] : $Settings['CreditControlFeeAct'];
	$Post = CreditControlPostDebtorTrans(CC_TYPE_WAIVER,
										$Charge['debtorno'],
										$Charge['amount'],
										__('Waiver of charge') . ' ' . $Charge['transno'] . ' - ' . $Reason,
										$Account,
										date('Y-m-d'),
										__('Waiver') . ' ' . $Charge['chargemonth'],
										$Trans['rate']);
	if ($Post === false) {
		return __('The customer has no branch to post the waiver to');
	}
	CreditControlAllocateCredit($Post['id'], $Charge['debtorno'], $Charge['amount'], array($Charge['transid']));
	DB_query("UPDATE latecharges
				SET status='W',
					waivetransno='" . $Post['transno'] . "',
					waivedby='" . $_SESSION['UserID'] . "',
					waiveddate=NOW(),
					waivereason='" . DB_escape_string(mb_substr($Reason, 0, 255)) . "'
				WHERE id='" . $Charge['id'] . "'");
	CreditControlLog($Charge['debtorno'],
		'WAIVER',
		__('Charge waived') . ' (' . $Charge['chargemonth'] . '): ' . $Reason,
		$Charge['amount'],
		$Charge['currcode'],
		CC_TYPE_WAIVER . '/' . $Post['transno']);
	return '';
}

/* Customers visible to the logged in user: a sales person's login only sees their own customers' credit information.
Returns SQL to add to a query on debtorsmaster ('' when there is no restriction). */
function CreditControlSalesmanLimitSQL() {
	if (isset($_SESSION['SalesmanLogin']) and $_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] != '') {
		return " AND debtorsmaster.debtorno IN (SELECT debtorno FROM custbranch WHERE salesman='" . $_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] . "') ";
	}
	return '';
}

/* True if the logged in user may see the credit information of the customer */
function CreditControlCanSeeCustomer($DebtorNo) {
	if (isset($_SESSION['SalesmanLogin']) and $_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] != '') {
		$Result = DB_query("SELECT debtorno FROM custbranch WHERE debtorno='" . $DebtorNo . "' AND salesman='" . $_SESSION['SalesmanLogin'] . "' LIMIT 1");
		return (DB_num_rows($Result) > 0);
	}
	return true;
}
